create.title: Hard-M1 t=1 high-height inverse-residue conductor reduction
create.statement_tex: Fix real X>=2, a literal middle or lower residual hard-M1 shell L>=2, sigma in {+1,-1}, fixed B>0, Q=H_B=floor((log(2X))^B), and a nonempty dyadic Y<h<=2Y with Y>H_B. On the exact accepted Round-185 primitive tangent-gcd carrier, expand the odd-U inverse-residue anchor with c_U(k)=2/[U{1+e(-k/U)}] and q_U(k)=U/(k,U), retaining the separate U=1 anchors and every literal selector, deletion, endpoint field, phase, and zero extension. The complete U=1 contribution, every exact conductor q_U(k)<=Q, every remaining mode with U<=4Q, and every remaining ordinary edge mode 0<|k|_U<=Q for U>4Q have total absolute size O_(B,epsilon)(L^2X^epsilon). The exact complementary one-outer-real-part aggregate has U>4Q, q_U(k)>Q, |k|_U>Q and positive capacity O_epsilon(YL^2X^epsilon); its one-sided O_(B,epsilon)(L^2X^epsilon) estimate is open. In u=gU,n=gh coordinates the low-conductor proof uses O(UL) literal atoms at fixed (kappa,u,U) and Fourier mass O((q/U)log(2q)). Centered primitive conductors self-return to the original orientation block, prime U returns literally, and the two near-half modes retain at least 8/pi^2 Fourier l2 mass. These are mechanism controls, not literal lower mass. This node proves only the strict transformed packet and exact reduction; it proves no complete high-h relation, complete t=1 residual, small-t owner, parent, bridge, theorem, or exponent.
